newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. invites Cypriot leaders to July 9 talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. invites Cypriot leaders to July 9 talks.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday issued invitations to leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities for direct talks on July 9, his envoy in divided Cyprus said.
Gustave Feissel said he had handed Annan's invitation to Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and was going to deliver a similar letter to Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash later on Wednesday.
"I gave a letter to Mr Clerides this morning and I plan to give a letter to Mr Denktash at 11.30," Feissel told Reuters.
Asked if the invitation was for talks on July 9, Feissel said: "This is correct."
The talks would be the first known encounter for nearly three years between Clerides and Denktash.
Annan told reporters in New York on Tuesday that the talks would be held outside New York.
Annan declined to comment on the forthcoming negotiations, aimed at reuniting the east Mediterranean island as a bi-communal, bi-communal federation.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkish troops occupied its northern third following a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Clerides's Greek Cypriot-led government is recognised internationally while Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state declared in 1983 and recognised only by Ankara.
